items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the penal law, in relation to increasing the penalties for sale of controlled substances on park grounds or playgrounds
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S994

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the penal law, in relation to
increasing the penalties for sale of controlled substances on park
grounds or playgrounds

PURPOSE:

To protect the safety of children and their families by providing
enhanced penalties for the sale of controlled substances on park
grounds and playgrounds.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of this bill adds a new subdivision 14-a to section 220.00
to the Penal Law to define "park grounds or playgrounds." Park grounds
or playgrounds is defined as any buildings, structures, playing
fields, playgrounds or lands that are owned, leased, or maintained by
the State, a municipality, a not for profit corporation, or other
similar entity and used on a regular basis as a recreation area. Any
parking lots, marinas, boat launches or parking garages that clearly
serve, and are within 1,000 feet of, a park ground or a playground are
also included in this definition.

Section two of this bill amends section 220.34 of the Penal Law,
criminal sale of a controlled substance in the fourth degree, to add
that a person is guilty of the offense if he or she sells a controlled
substance upon park grounds or playgrounds when there is evidence that
the person knew that the sale was occurring upon park grounds or a
playground. This amendment is added to the existing prohibition
against such sale of controlled substances on school grounds.

Section three of this bill amends section 220.44 of the Penal Law,
criminal sale of a controlled substance in or near school grounds, to
include the sale of controlled substances in or near park grounds or
playgrounds.

Section four of this bill provides that this act shall take effect on
the first of November next succeeding the date on which it shall have
become a law.

EXISTING LAW:

Current law penalizes persons who sell controlled substances on the
grounds of child day centers and educational facilities, but not park
grounds or playgrounds.

JUSTIFICATION:

The State of New York has consistently recognized that drug dealers
who target children are especially dangerous to society and, as such,
should be subjected to more severe penalties. This effort began in
1986 with Chapter 280, which targeted those who sell drugs upon or
near school grounds. In 1998, this was expanded to include sales of
controlled substances made upon the grounds of child day care or
educational facilities. In 2006, expanded these offenses to include


sales of controlled substances made on school buses. This legislation
would take an important next step by targeting those drug dealers who
lurk in public parks and playgrounds in an effort to prey on our
children.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2013-4: S.2173-A - Passed the Senate both years
2011- 2012: S.7152- Referred to Codes
2009- 2010: S.1568- Referred to Codes
2007- 2008: S.1777- Passed Senate both years
2005- 2006: S.1197- Passed Senate both years
2004: S.1504-A - Passed Senate
2003: S.1504 - Passed Senate

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect on the first of November next succeeding
the date on which it shall have become a law.

summary: Adds "park grounds and playgrounds" to statute currently providing increased penalties for sale of controlled substances to certain persons if such sale occurs on or within 1,000 feet of school grounds; defines "park ground or playgrounds" to mean in, or within any building or structure or any fields, lands or grounds owned, leased or maintained by the state, any agency or municipality thereof, etc., for the purposes of recreation or leisure.
title: Increases penalties for sale of controlled substances if it occurs on park grounds or playgrounds; defines park grounds or playgrounds
